mai: Heads-up — bringing up Zephyrus-v0.1 (Q4 quant profile) on staging caused a regression in our zh->en and ar->en evals. Need quick triage.
mai: Baseline (fp16) zh->en BLEU 28.7, zephyrus-int4 BLEU 24.2 on same eval set. ar->en BLEU dropped similarly (~4.1 pts).
mai: Repro script below, ran against staging model pool:
```
# repro (stash snapshot id: zephyrus-2026-03-18)
python eval/translate.py --model zephyrus-v0.1 --quant int4 --dataset bench/xx_to_en_1k.jsonl --batch 32 
```
mai: Quick check, outputs show lots of broken word boundaries in Chinese and stray brackets flipped in Arabic outputs. Example:
```
src: 他说：“我会去。”
fp16: He said, "I will go."
int4: He said , " I will go ."
```
mai: Arabic example: closing bracket ordering seems reversed in some sentences (looks bidi-related).

sasha: Interesting — could be tokenization mapping shift after quantized kernel selection or a detokenizer bug. Did we change tokenizer merges for zephyrus?
sasha: Can you paste the tokenized form for the Chinese example?

cheng: I ran tokenization + detok locally, here's token ids for the phrase (fp16 vs int4 run):
```
fp16 ids: [1024, 3582, 409, 12, 7833]
int4 ids: [1024, 3582, 409, 12, 7833]
```
cheng: ids are identical for that short example, so not a pure vocab shuffle.
cheng: But running longer samples I see occasional ZWJ (U+200D) and ZWNJ (U+200C) dropped when detok is applied after quantized runtime. Logs: `detok: removed U+200D at pos 42` repeated.

anil: Dropping ZWJ/ZWNJ would break CJK and some Arabic ligatures. Possibility: quantized runtime using a faster UTF-8 normalization path that accidentally strips zero-width chars.
anil: @ops-bot do we have a build tag for the int4 kernel that changed text normalization?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Can confirm: zephyrus-int4-staging used kernel-build tag `kernels/fast-detok-v2` deployed 2026-03-17 02:14UTC.
ops-bot: No other changes to tokenizer package version in that deploy.

mai: That matches suspicion — detok path in the runtime kernel. If detok path strips control chars to speed up, it might be acceptable for ascii-heavy languages but not for CJK/RTL.

sasha: Quick mitigation: re-run int4 with `--preserve-zwj` flag in detok and compare BLEU. If BLEU recovers, we have root cause.
sasha: I'll run a 1k eval with preserve flag now.

cheng: Also noticed bracket ordering issues for Arabic show up mostly when there are nested parentheses with punctuation. Might be an ordering/visual bidi reflow bug post-detok.
cheng: Adding a small patch to detok to skip reordering on strong RTL punctuation. Testing now.

anil: If we confirm kernel change is cause, rollout plan: pin int4 to previous detok kernel, block fast-detok-v2 for production, and run full regression suite.
anil: I'll open a rollback PR if sasha's test shows regressions fixed.

mai: Tasks: @sasha run preserve-zwj 1k eval, @cheng produce minimal failing example and open bug, @anil prepare rollback PR for kernels/fast-detok-v2.
mai: Ping me when you have the BLEU numbers. :eyes:

sasha: Running now, ETA ~12m.
sasha: quick note — dev eval runner shows candidate BLEU (preserve-zwj) = 28.5 for zh->en on same set.
sasha: Looks promising.

cheng: I reproduced bracket flip locally, opened issue #4126 with minimal repro and diff from detok logs. PR for skip-reorder attached to issue.

anil: Started rollback branch and smoke canary to previous kernel build. Will run smoke on a small traffic slice.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary for `kernels/fast-detok-v2` rollback started at 2026-03-18T12:05Z to group staging-canary-1.

mai: Great. If preserve-zwj fixes BLEU we can treat this as a detok policy regression in the kernel. We'll need an integration test to ensure zero-width characters and bidi punctuation survive quantized fast paths.

sasha: Agreed. I'll add a test case to the eval harness (zwj/zwnj + bidi brackets) so this doesn't regress silently.

mai: Thanks team. Keep updates in this thread and tag me on PRs. :thumbsup:
